haiku-low.q1: They do not differ. Both return 401 with the login page saying "Invalid email or password" and no cookie. An unknown email is still checked against the dummy hash.
haiku-low.q2: It gets 429 with the lock message "Too many failed attempts. Try again in 15 minutes." The password is not checked and no failure row is written.
haiku-low.q3: The session the browser's sid cookie points to is deleted in the login transaction. A new session with a new ID replaces it. Other devices' sessions are left alone.
haiku-low.q4: The cookie holds only the session's random 256-bit ID. It is HttpOnly, so page scripts cannot read it. It is also Secure and SameSite=Lax.
haiku-low.q5: The session stops working 12 hours after login, even if the user is active. The 30-minute idle timeout restarts with each request but cannot run past the absolute time.
haiku-low.q6: It clears the sid cookie and redirects to /login. It does not serve the page or delete the expired row; the cleanup job removes it later.
haiku-low.q7: The server deletes the sessions row matching the sid cookie before replying. If no session exists, nothing is deleted. Either way it clears the cookie and redirects to /login.
haiku-low.q8: Session state is kept in the Postgres sessions table. Any instance finds it by looking up the cookie's ID there, since the instances share no memory.
haiku-low.q9: Failures are kept as login_failures rows in Postgres, one per failed attempt. The server counts rows whose failed_at is within the last 10 minutes by the Postgres clock.
haiku-low.q10: It checks that the sessions row with the cookie's ID has idle and absolute expiry times later than the Postgres clock. If valid, it sets idle_expires_at to the earlier of now plus 30 minutes or absolute_expires_at.
haiku-low.q11: The browser gets 503 with "Sign-in is temporarily unavailable. Try again shortly." No cookie is set, and the transaction rolls back so the old session stays.
haiku-low.q12: The cleanup job in each instance, running every 10 minutes, deletes sessions past either expiry time. Idle sessions also expire on their own at 30 minutes without requests.

sonnet.q1: They don't differ. Both get 401 and the login page with "Invalid email or password", no cookie. (A dummy bcrypt check keeps timing the same.)
sonnet.q2: If the email is locked, it gets 429 with the lock message ("Too many failed attempts. Try again in 15 minutes."). The password is not checked and no failure row is written. The lock lasts 15 minutes from the 5th failure.
sonnet.q3: In one transaction the session the incoming sid cookie points to is deleted, and a new session with a new random ID is created (and the email's failure rows are cleared). If the transaction fails, it rolls back and the old session stays.
sonnet.q4: Only the session's random 256-bit ID. Page scripts cannot read it, because it is HttpOnly. It is also Secure and SameSite=Lax.
sonnet.q5: At 12 hours after login (the absolute timeout). Activity keeps resetting the 30-minute idle timeout, but the idle expiry is capped at the absolute expiry.
sonnet.q6: It clears the sid cookie and redirects to /login. The user is not sent back to the page they asked for.
sonnet.q7: The sessions row for the sid cookie is deleted, if one exists, and this is done before the reply goes out. If none exists it does nothing. The reply (clear cookie, redirect to /login) is the same either way.
sonnet.q8: In the Postgres sessions table, which both instances share. The instance looks up the row whose id equals the sid cookie value.
sonnet.q9: In the Postgres login_failures table, with one row (email, failed_at) per failed attempt. The server counts that email's rows with failed_at within the last 10 minutes, measured by the Postgres clock (now()), not an instance clock.
sonnet.q10: It compares the session's idle_expires_at and absolute_expires_at against the Postgres clock. Both must be later. It writes back idle_expires_at, set to the earlier of (Postgres clock + 30 minutes) and absolute_expires_at.
sonnet.q11: A 503 with the login page saying "Sign-in is temporarily unavailable. Try again shortly." No cookie is set. The transaction rolls back, so the old session is untouched.
sonnet.q12: The cleanup job. Each instance runs it every 10 minutes and deletes sessions rows past either expiry time.
